name: BMKG Indonesia open weather and earthquake data
short: Indonesia's official 3-day village weather forecast, weather nowcast alerts and latest earthquakes. Free, no key.
summary: BMKG, Indonesia's meteorology, climatology and geophysics agency, publishes open JSON: a 3-day forecast at 3-hour steps for any administrative level-IV area (kelurahan or village) via api.bmkg.go.id, the latest earthquake and lists of felt and M5+ quakes via data.bmkg.go.id, and an RSS feed of nowcast weather alerts. The pages state a limit of 60 requests per minute per IP and require showing BMKG as the source. The forecast is produced twice a day, so it is a forecast, not a live reading; the earthquake files update with each event (the newest sampled was under 8 hours old at the call).

tasks: 3-day weather forecast per village: temperature, humidity, cloud cover, wind, visibility
latest earthquake with magnitude, depth, region, tsunami potential and felt report (autogempa)
15 latest M5.0+ and 15 latest felt earthquakes

coverage.notes: Forecast is addressed by Ministry of Home Affairs level-IV administrative codes (adm4); the example is Kemayoran, Jakarta (31.71.03.1001). Weather text fields are Indonesian with an English field. Quake data covers Indonesia and its surrounding seas.

rate_limit.notes: Stated on the forecast and earthquake documentation pages.

delivery.basis: Earthquake files update on each event (earthquake page); the latest sampled event was 17:38 UTC on 2026-11-06 and the call was 18:2x UTC. The forecast updates 2 times a day (forecast page), so it is a forecast rather than a reading.

latency.typical: minutes for quakes, 12 hours for forecasts
latency.notes: Quake page gives no fixed interval. Forecast: 2 updates per day, 8 points per day at 3-hour steps.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes after a quake; forecasts up to half a day
freshness.notes: Each forecast carries analysis_date; each quake a UTC DateTime.

licensing.summary: BMKG's documentation pages require BMKG to be credited as the data source and shown in your app or system. They state no licence and no other terms; the earthquake page tells users to write to support[at]bmkg.go.id for certainty about terms of use. Redistribution, resale and AI use are therefore Not stated. Rate limit 60 requests per minute per IP.

time.method: Quake DateTime in UTC; forecast utc_datetime.
time.unknown: UTC DateTime fields in earthquake files, analysis_date on forecasts; clock handling not documented.

location.method: Quake Coordinates field; forecast lokasi lat/lon.
location.unknown: Quake coordinates are BMKG's computed epicentres; forecast areas carry lat/lon of the village.

content.method: Magnitude, depth, region, tsunami potential, MMI felt scale.
content.unknown: Preliminary automatic quake solutions (the sampled one is M3.3 with felt report); forecasts are model output, not observations.

human.unknown: Not applicable: automated instruments and official forecasts, not people.

application.unknown: No signing or attestation from instrument to API is documented.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing documented independently confirms individual readings.

endpoints.notes: Latest earthquake; also gempaterkini.json (15 M5+) and gempadirasakan.json (15 felt).

sources.claim: Forecast API: endpoint, adm4 parameter, 3-day 3-hour fields, 2 updates per day, 60 requests/min/IP, BMKG attribution required, no licence stated, no key mentioned
Earthquake files autogempa/gempaterkini/gempadirasakan, update on each event, 60 requests/min/IP, attribution required, contact support[at]bmkg.go.id for terms
Data sections listed: forecast, earthquakes, nowcast; contact support[at]bmkg.go.id
